## Open

### F-133 — The generated fixture is destroyed while the test runner may read it

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-kukum · open_

`e2e.test.ts` regenerates `test/fixture/e2e-realm/` by deleting the tree first, and tap also
collects that fixture's own `index.test.ts` as part of the package suite, so the fixture is rebuilt
while the runner may be reading it. A `SIGTERM` part-way through left it empty and produced three
cascading failures: `Cannot find module '…/test/fixture/e2e-realm/index.test.ts'`, plus failures in
`e2e.test.ts` itself (`time=410262ms`) and in `index.test.ts`.

The same race appears without a kill, because `blong-dev test` runs tap in parallel: one run
reported `Cannot find module '.../browser-test.ts'` and 'no tests found' while the file was present
on disk, and the next run was green. When a fixture test fails, re-run it before investigating, and
`ls` before believing the message.

This is a latent race in the fixture design, not just redundancy. Generate into a sibling directory
and swap it into place, so a reader only ever sees a complete tree.

## Resolved

### F-122 — A record-driven route map collapsed onto one empty key

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-kukum · resolved_

`blong-kukum` builds its ~70 validations programmatically and returns them from a `validation()`
export. `Registry._validations()` takes the route key from the function's `.name` and not from the
object key, because that is how `blong-mock.validation(models)` works. JavaScript's
`SetFunctionName` only fires for a function literal assigned directly to a property, so building the
map with `result[method] = entry(method)` leaves `.name === ''`: every route collapsed onto one
empty key and the gateway served a bogus `/rpc//` route that answered 401.

Setting the name explicitly with `Object.defineProperty(fn, 'name', {value: method})` fixed it. The
map was found by temporarily logging the validations inside `Gateway.route`. When a record-driven
API surface 'exists but is unreachable', check the function names before anything else.

### F-123 — `realm add` needs a single-word realm name

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-kukum · resolved_

The `blong-kopi` template substitutes `$subject` into identifiers — `browser-test.ts` carries a
`$subject:` object key — and derives seed method names from `<subject><Object>Merge`. `demo-realm`
produced a syntax error, and `demoRealm` produced a realm whose test seed dispatched to the
non-existent `demo.realm.thingMerge`; `demo` works. `blong realm <name>` has the same constraint but
failed later and less clearly, so the `realm` primitive now rejects multi-word names up front.

### F-124 — Nested `${...}` in a generator template literal fails only downstream

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-kukum · resolved_

Emitting a literal `${current}` from inside a template literal needs an escaped `${`, and
`${${object}Id}` needs both escaped. Getting the backslash count wrong does not fail loudly: the
outer generator still parses, and the error surfaces only when the generated artifact is read
(`Unexpected token '{'`, pointing at the generator rather than at the artifact). Node's
type-stripper reports the whole generator module as unparseable, which reads like a syntax error in
code that is fine.

Do not escape nested placeholders. Build them at runtime instead (`'$' + '{' + ctx.object + 'Id}'`)
and interpolate the result: that removes the escaping entirely, and the generated text is verifiable
in one command.

### F-125 — A failing test can encode the behavior you are replacing

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-kukum · resolved_

Renaming the shared-file overwrite to a merge left `operations.test.ts`'s test 'add warns when a
shared file is replaced' failing. The test was not wrong when it was written — it pinned the old
contract.

When a failing test describes exactly the behavior being changed, rewrite it to the new contract
plus a case for the old one under `--replace`, rather than deleting it.

### F-126 — A generator bug that only running the artifact can find

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-kukum · resolved_

The `schema`/`table` template emitted `constraints: {primaryKey: ['xId'], index: [['xName']]}` —
array shapes the framework does not accept. It fails at none of the earlier gates: generation,
typecheck and import are all clean, and the failure appears only at table creation, as an index over
a column named `0`:

```sql
alter table `shop_gadget` add index `shop_gadget_idx_0`(`0`)
```

The canonical shape is object-keyed (`unique: {name: {}}`, `index: {column: {}}`), as `blong-kopi`'s
own `meta/type/schema.ts` shows.

### F-131 — Regenerating a template over an extended realm reverts the additions

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-kukum · resolved_

`planTemplate` rewrites every template file, so regenerating the fixture in place reverted the
composed additions (`index.ts`, `browser-test.ts`, `meta/db/db.ts` and the Playwright spec) before
re-applying them. The property worth asserting is therefore reproducibility of a fresh generation,
not in-place idempotency. Two further gaps surfaced the same way: the generated test seed never
granted the entity's actions in the realm's RBAC seed, so the browser leg was denied 403 through the
gateway, and non-code artifacts (`.yaml`, `.sql`) counted as hand-written because the generated
marker is a TypeScript sentinel, which left a seed permanently unrefreshable.

Treat template regeneration as a rewrite rather than a merge. The package now keeps generated files
out of version control and locks the generators with the committed Playwright baselines.

### F-132 — A screenshot baseline captured live data and would fail the next run

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-kukum · resolved_

The generated Playwright spec called `browseModel` without `searchText`, so the browse screenshot
showed the whole table, including the `ENT-TEST-<timestamp>` rows the tap suites had just created.
The test passed when the baseline was written and would have failed on the next run, which is the
worst shape a visual test can have.

A generated `browseModel` call must pin a seeded marker — the realm template uses
`searchText: 'Sample $Object One'` — because a baseline with anything time-dependent in it is not a
baseline. The seed row name now comes from one shared helper, so the seed and the spec cannot drift
apart.

### F-134 — A generated test paged an unbounded table and failed once it grew

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-kukum · resolved_

The fixture's `widget find` failure had nothing to do with master-detail entities, PK types or the
framework. The generated test did `find({paging: {pageNumber: 1, pageSize: 100}})` and asserted that
the row it had just added was in the result; rows come back in ascending PK order and the table is
never cleaned up, so once it passed 100 rows the new row moved to page 2 and the assertion failed.
`gadget` passed only because its table still held 96 rows — it was racing the same bug.

Two things made this hard to see: the failure is data-dependent, so it reads as flakiness, and the
first database queried was `e2e-realm-kalin`, a stale name from an older scheme, where the real one
is `blong-e2e-kalin`, derived from the suite name passed to `load()`.

A generated test that asserts membership in a `find` result must filter by the unique value it just
created (`filterBy: {name}`), never page an unbounded table.

### F-135 — Moving a module one folder deeper changed its `import.meta.url` depth

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-kukum · resolved_

`REALM_TEMPLATE_ROOT` is `../blong-kopi` resolved from the package root, but had to become
`../../blong-kopi` once the module moved into `operations/`. A relative URL built from
`import.meta.url` is depth-sensitive, so every move of the file that computes it has to be checked.

### F-136 — Renaming a binding to `find` collided with a local of the same name

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-kukum · resolved_

Renaming a binding to `find`, `get` or `tree` collides with local variables of the same name in
tests: `const find = build(find)` is a self-reference. The local was renamed instead.
